gold_answer.verdict: no — use an alternative P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor) if no contraindication
gold_answer.cited_guideline: CPIC@2022 (Lee et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2022;112:959-967, PMID 35034351)
gold_answer.rationale: CYP2C19 IMs have reduced active metabolite formation, less platelet inhibition, and increased risk of MACE on clopidogrel after ACS/PCI. The 2022 CPIC update strengthened the recommendation to avoid clopidogrel in IMs in this setting.

q05.question: A patient with metastatic colorectal cancer is about to start 5-fluorouracil/leucovorin. DPYD genotyping reveals heterozygous c.1905+1G>A (DPYD*2A); all other tested DPYD variants are wild-type. What starting-dose modification is indicated?

gold_answer.cited_guideline: CPIC@2017 (Amstutz et al., Clin Pharmacol Ther 2018;103:210-216, PMID 29152729) with November 2018 CPIC update
gold_answer.rationale: DPYD*2A is a no-function variant (activity 0). A heterozygous carrier has activity score 1, conferring intermediate metabolizer status. The 2017 CPIC guideline as updated in 2018 recommends a 50% starting-dose reduction in DPYD intermediate metabolizers, then titrate by toxicity.

gold_answer.verdict: osimertinib (single agent) is the preferred first-line systemic therapy (Category 1); osimertinib + platinum-pemetrexed is a Category 1 alternative based on FLAURA2
gold_answer.cited_guideline: NCCN NSCLC Guidelines v3.2024 (Category 1); FDA label for osimertinib (Tagrisso); FLAURA / FLAURA2 trials
gold_answer.rationale: EGFR exon 19 deletion is a sensitizing mutation. The FLAURA trial established osimertinib superiority over earlier-generation EGFR TKIs in PFS and OS, making it the NCCN preferred first-line regimen. PD-L1 status does not change the recommendation in driver-positive NSCLC; first-line single-agent immunotherapy is not preferred over osimertinib.

Tumor testing shows mismatch-repair deficient (dMMR) / microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) status by IHC and PCR. Is pembrolizumab an FDA-approved option, and what was the original tumor-agnostic basis?

gold_answer.verdict: yes — pembrolizumab is FDA-approved for unresectable or metastatic MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors that have progressed on prior therapy; this was the first tumor-agnostic FDA approval (23 May 2017)
gold_answer.cited_guideline: FDA accelerated approval 23 May 2017 (converted to full approval 2023) — pembrolizumab for MSI-H/dMMR solid tumors; KEYNOTE-016, -164, -012, -028, -158
gold_answer.rationale: MSI-H/dMMR tumors carry high mutational load and are highly responsive to PD-1 blockade across tissue origins. The KEYNOTE basket trials supported a tissue-agnostic approval — a regulatory first.

q21.question: A 30-year-old woman of Northern European ancestry presents for preconception carrier screening. Her CFTR sequencing returns p.Phe508del (F508del) heterozygote (one copy). Her partner has not yet been tested. What is the appropriate next step per ACMG?

gold_answer.verdict: she is a CF carrier; offer partner CFTR carrier screening (with the ACMG-recommended ≥100-variant minimum panel) and provide genetic counseling about reproductive options if both partners carry pathogenic variants
gold_answer.cited_guideline: ACMG Updated CFTR Carrier Screening Recommendations 2023 (Deignan et al., Genet Med 2023;25(8):100867); ACOG Committee Opinion 690/691
gold_answer.rationale: F508del is a well-established CF-causing variant. ACMG (2023) recommends a minimum CFTR variant set of 100 variants for carrier screening, replacing the older 23-variant panel; if one member of a couple is a carrier, partner testing is essential to estimate reproductive risk and inform options including PGT-M and prenatal diagnosis.

scoring_rubric.verdict_correct: recommends partner CFTR carrier screening AND identifies the woman as a CF carrier

q22.question: A 32-year-old woman has SMN1 carrier testing showing 1 copy of SMN1 (and 2 copies of SMN2). Her partner's SMN1 testing shows 1 copy of SMN1. What is the per-pregnancy risk of an affected child with spinal muscular atrophy, assuming standard biallelic SMN1 deletion is the cause, and what counseling/options should be offered?

required_inputs.clinical_context: preconception couple, both confirmed SMN1 carriers

gold_answer.verdict: 1-in-4 (25%) per-pregnancy risk of an affected child; offer genetic counseling, PGT-M, prenatal diagnostic testing (CVS or amniocentesis with SMN1 copy-number analysis), and discussion of newborn-screening implications
gold_answer.cited_guideline: ACMG 2008 SMA carrier-screening recommendation; ACMG 2021 carrier-screening tiered guidance (Gregg et al., Genet Med 2021;23:1793, PMID 34285390); ACOG Committee Opinion 691
gold_answer.rationale: Both parents have a single SMN1 copy and are carriers of the canonical biallelic SMN1 deletion. By Mendelian inheritance, each pregnancy has a 25% risk of homozygous SMN1 deletion (affected SMA). SMN2 copy number modifies severity but does not alter affected probability.

scoring_rubric.verdict_correct: states "1-in-4" or "25%" recurrence risk AND mentions counseling / reproductive options

q31.question: A 38-year-old asymptomatic woman has a germline BRCA1 pathogenic variant (c.5266dupC, p.Q1756Pfs*74) identified on multi-gene panel testing. She has completed childbearing. What is the NCCN-recommended risk-reducing surgery for ovarian/tubal cancer, and at what age?

gold_answer.verdict: risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) recommended typically between ages 35-40 years (after completion of childbearing); risk-reducing mastectomy can also be discussed for breast cancer risk
gold_answer.cited_guideline: NCCN Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment: Breast, Ovarian, and Pancreatic v3.2024
gold_answer.rationale: BRCA1 carriers face ~40-60% lifetime risk of ovarian/tubal/peritoneal cancer with onset typically in the 40s. NCCN recommends RRSO at 35-40 years for BRCA1 (vs. 40-45 for BRCA2), as data show major mortality benefit. RRSO removes ovaries and fallopian tubes; salpingectomy alone is not a recommended substitute.

scoring_rubric.verdict_correct: recommends RRSO (risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy) at age 35-40 years for BRCA1

q34.question: A 44-year-old man has a germline TP53 pathogenic missense variant identified on cascade testing after his sister was diagnosed with early-onset breast cancer. He is asymptomatic. What surveillance program is recommended for this Li-Fraumeni Syndrome carrier?

gold_answer.verdict: comprehensive Li-Fraumeni surveillance: annual whole-body MRI; annual brain MRI; annual breast MRI ± mammography for women starting age 20-30; annual abdominal/pelvic ultrasound; clinical examinations every 6-12 months including skin and neurological; colonoscopy every 2-5 years starting age 25; targeted blood work; counseling about cancer-syndrome-related symptoms
gold_answer.cited_guideline: NCCN Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment: Breast, Ovarian, and Pancreatic v3.2024 (LFS section); Toronto/IARC LFS surveillance protocol (Villani et al.); 'Chompret' criteria
gold_answer.rationale: TP53 carriers face very high cumulative cancer risk (~70% by age 30 in men, ~100% by age 70). Annual whole-body MRI plus brain MRI is the cornerstone of LFS surveillance — supported by prospective Toronto cohort data showing improved 5-year survival for screened vs unscreened individuals.

scoring_rubric.guideline_cited_with_version: includes "NCCN" with version OR "Toronto protocol" or "Villani"

q43.question: A 60-year-old patient with metastatic CRC is starting irinotecan-based chemotherapy. UGT1A1 genotyping reveals UGT1A1 *28/*28 (homozygous TA7/TA7). What dose modification is supported by the FDA label?

gold_answer.verdict: reduce irinotecan starting dose by at least one dose level; 70% of standard dose is a commonly cited target (DPWG); subsequent doses titrated to tolerance / neutrophil count
gold_answer.cited_guideline: Camptosar (irinotecan) FDA prescribing information (UGT1A1 section); DPWG 2018 (Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group); Onivyde (liposomal irinotecan) FDA label (recommends initial 50 mg/m^2)
